mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% in three months signals an improving labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) by more than 5% in two months signals a strengthening housing market, which boosts the economy and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a weakening supply side, which may lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 70% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same period, it signals a robust labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% in a month and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (change within ±0.2%), it signals strong demand without inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% and CPIAUCSL changes within ±0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% in three months, coupled with a stable or decreasing GDP (GDPC1), signals a tightening monetary policy without corresponding economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases > 0.5% and GDPC1 is stable or decreases in 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in two months signals a strong supply side, which boosts economic growth and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when the signal is active.
